status: proposal; no model was run for this list; every memory figure is an estimate [I] until measured

reference_machine.gpu: NVIDIA GTX 1070, 8192 MiB; about 2700 MiB used by the desktop, about 5490 MiB free (doc 44)
reference_machine.runtime: llama.cpp llama-server; Vulkan build (Plotroom's own target); CUDA 12.x build as a comparison for the MoE-offload rows (CUDA 13 dropped Pascal)

order: 1. Re-run the doc 44 baselines on the same llama-server build (Ollama numbers are not comparable across runtimes)
2. Priority A rows (1-4) on the reference GPU
3. Priority B/C rows (5-9) as the 4-6 GB and CPU-only tiers, then the doc 14 carry-overs
4. Optional, owner's call: the 'bonsai' paired probe (Bonsai 2 27B on the PrismML fork against Qwen3.8-27B UD-IQ2_XXS on mainline), only after the Priority A rows
notes: --fit is on by default and adjusts only unset arguments (1024 MiB margin); set -ngl, --n-cpu-moe and -c explicitly and record the effective values from the server log
-np 1 keeps the whole 8192-token context for one request
run.py sends chat_template_kwargs {enable_thinking: false} and records thinking_chars; for a template that ignores it, start the server with --reasoning off
Record nvidia-smi before and after load, host working set for offload rows, cold and warm load, prompt-processing and generation tokens/s
Sampler pinned identically for every model (run.py flags in PIN); the per-suite temperature comes from run.py (0.6 pick/fill/text, 0.2 explain)
Download each file from its pinned url and check the SHA-256 before starting the server

notes: b10743 contains fork PRs #206 (PQ2_0 AVX2 CPU kernels), #238 (Vulkan PQ2_0 no longer silently on the CPU), #245 (AVX-512 load crash), #248 (PTQ1_0 SSE2/SSSE3 CPU kernels) and #271 (CPU variants in the CUDA bundles) [V, GitHub compare API]; not #250 (PTQ1_0 AVX2, in review)
unpack into its own folder; never replace the mainline b11146 build that the other rows use
the release has Vulkan, CPU, CUDA and HIP builds but no SYCL build; #238 in b10743 carries #188's Vulkan PQ2_0 support and the PTQ1_0 integer-dot decode kernel that fork issue #247 measured
the fork's llama-server has --fit on by default (1,024 MiB margin, adjusts only unset arguments); set -ngl, -ot and -c explicitly and record the effective split from the log
do not use the CUDA 13.x builds: no Pascal target, and 13.3 exits silently on some Windows systems (KNOWN_ISSUES, fork issue #222)

the CUDA 12.4 arm is a comparison only, since Plotroom's own builds never bundle CUDA (D022 decision 2); it carries sm_61 as 61-virtual code that the driver compiles on first start, so the first load is slow
check each zip against the SHA-256 digest above (the digest GitHub lists for the asset) before unpacking

a_partial_gpu_vulkan.expected_vram: [I] keep total use below the ~5,490 MiB free: about 4.3-4.5 GiB of weights (the file minus the ~265 MiB token embedding, which llama.cpp always keeps on the CPU, minus 12 blocks) + KV 512 MiB at 8K f16 + about 150 MiB of Gated DeltaNet state + compute buffers; start with the last 12 of 64 blocks in RAM
a_partial_gpu_vulkan.expected_host_ram: [I] about 0.95 GiB for the 12 CPU blocks (about 80 MiB each: 24.35B backbone parameters x 1.75 bits / 64 blocks) plus the ~265 MiB token embedding, served from the memory-mapped file
a_partial_gpu_vulkan.bench_first: llama-bench -m Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PTQ1_0.gguf -ngl 99 -ot "blk\.(5[2-9]|6[0-3])\.=CPU" -t 4 -fa 1 -p 512 -n 128 -r 2  # the fork's llama-bench README documents -ot
a_partial_gpu_vulkan.tuning: [I] keep -ngl 99 and move whole blocks with -ot, so the CPU blocks are named explicitly and every layer's KV cache and recurrent state stays on the GPU (a lower -ngl would also offload the output layer first, then the last blocks: src/llama-model.cpp); if nvidia-smi shows more than ~300 MiB left after the first request, return one block to the GPU (blk\.(5[3-9]|6[0-3])\. is 11 blocks); if loading fails or use exceeds the free VRAM, add one (blk\.(5[1-9]|6[0-3])\.); record the final pattern and the CPU and Vulkan0 model buffer sizes from the server log
a_partial_gpu_vulkan.kv_variant: -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -fa on saves about 240 MiB at 8K [I], worth one to three more blocks on the GPU
a_partial_gpu_vulkan.expected_speed: [I] generation about 3-6 tokens/s in llama-bench, lower in llama-server; prompt processing at or below the ~16 tokens/s measured with the whole model on a GTX 1070 (fork issue #247) [V], so at least 60 s per 1,000 uncached prompt tokens; a Pick (about 200 uncached tokens, doc 46 section 2.6) takes about 15-20 s

a2_partial_gpu_cuda_12_4_optional.file: PTQ1_0 (PQ2_0 as a second try: it has a Pascal tile configuration for prompt processing and AVX2 kernels for its CPU blocks)
a2_partial_gpu_cuda_12_4_optional.llama_server: llama-server -m Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PTQ1_0.gguf -ngl 99 -ot "blk\.(5[2-9]|6[0-3])\.=CPU" -t 4 --jinja -c 8192 -np 1 --no-mmproj --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080  # the CUDA 12.4 zip's llama-server, with cudart unpacked beside it
a2_partial_gpu_cuda_12_4_optional.expected_speed: [U] unmeasured on Pascal; PTQ1_0 prompt processing there falls back to dequantise plus cuBLAS (its batched kernel needs Turing); the first-generation ternary 27B ran pp512 278 and tg128 20.5 tokens/s on a GTX 1080 Ti (CUDA), but as a Q2_0 file without the Hadamard rotation, wholly on an 11 GB card, so treat it as an upper bound
a2_partial_gpu_cuda_12_4_optional.note: a bring-your-own comparison only; a much faster result supports documenting the fork as a bring-your-own endpoint for NVIDIA users, not managing it

b_cpu_only.file: PQ2_0 (b10743 has AVX2 kernels for PQ2_0, #206, but only SSE2/SSSE3 for PTQ1_0, #248)
b_cpu_only.runtime: the fork's win-cpu-x64 zip, or the Vulkan zip with -dev none
b_cpu_only.expected_host_ram: [I] about 7.5-8 GiB (7.21 GB of weights + 512 MiB of KV + about 150 MiB of state + buffers)
b_cpu_only.expected_speed: [I] generation about 1-3 tokens/s (38.4 GB/s over 7.21 GB caps it at 5.3); prompt processing a few tokens/s
b_cpu_only.scope: a speed data point only: llama-bench -m Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PQ2_0.gguf -dev none -t 4 -p 512 -n 64 -r 1, plus one fill call (--limit 1 --k 1); not a harness candidate

bonsai.request_settings: thinking off: run.py sends chat_template_kwargs {enable_thinking: false}, which this template honours by emitting an empty think block [V]; leave the server's --reasoning at its default (auto), because --reasoning on overrides a client's off switch (KNOWN_ISSUES); run.py sends exactly one system message, first, as the template requires; never send reasoning_effort 'high' (HTTP 500); check one --dry-run, then one real call for parse_ok and thinking_chars == 0
bonsai.sampler: the common pin (--top-k 20 --top-p 0.95 --min-p 0 --presence-penalty 0 --repeat-penalty 1.0, with run.py's per-suite temperature), identical for the comparator; the card's non-thinking values (temperature 0.7, top_p 0.80, top_k 20, min_p 0, presence_penalty 1.5) are not used, so the two arms stay comparable; the GGUF's own general.sampling values are the thinking-mode ones
run: python tools/local-qual/run.py --backend llamacpp --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --suite fill --k 1 --limit 3 --warmup --timeout 900 --out results/bonsai-gate__fill.jsonl --top-k 20 --top-p 0.95 --min-p 0 --presence-penalty 0 --repeat-penalty 1.0  # speed and loop gate; read prompt_n, timings and thinking_chars
python tools/local-qual/run.py --backend llamacpp --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --suite fill --k 3 --timeout 900 --top-k 20 --top-p 0.95 --min-p 0 --presence-penalty 0 --repeat-penalty 1.0

python tools/local-qual/run.py --backend llamacpp --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --suite text --condition none --k 2 --timeout 900 --top-k 20 --top-p 0.95 --min-p 0 --presence-penalty 0 --repeat-penalty 1.0

python tools/local-qual/run.py --backend llamacpp --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --suite explain --condition cards --k 2 --timeout 900 --top-k 20 --top-p 0.95 --min-p 0 --presence-penalty 0 --repeat-penalty 1.0

python tools/local-qual/run.py --backend llamacpp --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --suite pick-hard --condition none --k 3 --timeout 900 --top-k 20 --top-p 0.95 --min-p 0 --presence-penalty 0 --repeat-penalty 1.0

python tools/local-qual/run.py --backend llamacpp --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --suite pick-hard --condition cards --k 3 --timeout 900 --top-k 20 --top-p 0.95 --min-p 0 --presence-penalty 0 --repeat-penalty 1.0
python tools/local-qual/score.py
bonsai.expected_wall_time: [I] roughly 1.5-2.5 hours per arm for the four suites (256 calls) at ~16 tokens/s of prompt processing: pick-hard is 180 calls at about 15-20 s (45-60 min); fill (36 calls), explain (20) and text (20) at about 30-80 s each add about 40-100 min; the comparator should take well under half of that if its prompt processing reaches 30-60 tokens/s
stop_rules: stop and record if a gate call shows thinking_chars > 0 or fails parse_ok

stop and record if the server log shows a grammar parse failure ('failed to parse grammar'), or an answer ignores the schema (fork issue #87: a grammar that fails to compile is logged and generation continues unconstrained; reported for tool-call grammars)
stop if more than 1 of the first 10 calls hits the per-suite output cap (looping)
if llama-bench shows pp512 below 10 tokens/s or tg128 below 2 tokens/s, run fill and text only and skip pick-hard

comparator_mainline.name: Qwen3.8-27B UD-IQ2_XXS (Unsloth)
comparator_mainline.why: the same base as Bonsai 2 and nearly the size of PQ2_0 (7.27 against 7.21 GB); runs on the installed mainline b11146 Vulkan build that Plotroom ships; fork issue #283 used this file as the conventional 2-bit comparator, and PrismML's table lists an IQ2_XXS of the same 7.27 GB
comparator_mainline.runtime: mainline llama.cpp b11146 Vulkan (the build tools/local-qual used)
comparator_mainline.tuning: [I] start with the last 22 of 64 blocks in RAM and adjust one block at a time as for arm a; --fit is on by default in mainline but adjusts only unset arguments, so record the effective split from the log
comparator_mainline.expected_host_ram: [I] about 2.5-3 GiB of CPU-resident weights beyond the mapped file
comparator_mainline.expected_speed: [I] generation about 5-8 tokens/s (about 4.5 GB on the GPU at the ~128 GB/s implied by doc 46's Qwen3.5-4B Vulkan tg32 44.0 on 2.91 GB, plus about 2 GB on the CPU at 15-25 GB/s); prompt processing unmeasured, about 30-60 tokens/s by scaling the 4B's pp256 of 382-389
comparator_mainline.request_settings: send enable_thinking false (Qwen3.8 thinks by default), as run.py does; the same sampler pin
comparator_mainline.run: the same run.py commands as the Bonsai arm; records and file names default to the served GGUF's name, so the arms do not collide

optional_mainline_curiosity.name: Bonsai-27B Q1_0 (first generation, Qwen3.6-27B base)
optional_mainline_curiosity.runtime: mainline b11146 Vulkan (Q1_0 on Vulkan since PR #21539)
optional_mainline_curiosity.expected_vram: [V-vendor] peak 5.2 GB at 4K and 5.6 GB at 10K context (decimal GB, FP16 KV); [I] fits the ~5,490 MiB free at 8K, tightly (about 5,215 MiB interpolated), with less than doc 44's proposed 512 MiB margin above 4K
optional_mainline_curiosity.scope: speed only (llama-bench -p 512 -n 128), one --dry-run and a fill gate (--limit 3); its vendor quality is thinking-mode only (89.5% of Qwen3.6-27B FP16), and one hands-on report got a false answer with thinking off

bonsai.decision: Bonsai earns a place over the comparator only if it leads by doc 44 section 6's noise rule on Fill all-validators pass^3 or on text grader passes, and passes the escape must-pass (doc 47 section 6.3 item 6). Neither arm earns a local badge on this box unless it meets section 6.3 item 3's offload bar (whole-record Fill pass^3 >= 0.8, p90 fill latency <= 10 s warm), which ~16 tokens/s of prompt processing cannot. A clear Bonsai lead would support listing it as a bring-your-own model for newer GPUs, not managing the fork (doc 47 section 2.7).
